text.p: GreenPoint Financial Corp chairman and chief executive Thomas Johnson said in a telephone interview he is "reasonably comfortable" with the First Call consensus earnings estimate of $3.44 for 1997.

Earlier Wednesday, GreenPoint reported 1996 earnings rose to $3.02 per share from 1995's $2.29. Fourth-quarter 1996 earnings rose to $0.81 per share from $0.42. The First Call consensus view for the 1996 fourth quarter was $0.79 per share.
Johnson said the year-over-year gains for 1996 reflected both the acquisition of Home Savings branches and the national introduction of GreenPoint's "No Doc" mortgage product.

GreenPoint originated $2.4 billion in mortgages in 1996 compared to $1.0 billion in 1995. More than half of the 1996 volume was outside the New York area where GreenPoint has its headquarters and an extensive branch network.

The product, which requires no documentation by borrowers, was introduced in Chicago, Philadelphia, Boston, Miami and Washington D.C. GreenPoint aims to enter San Francisco, Denver, Phoenix, Atlanta and Seattle in 1997.

Asked how GreenPoint was competing successfully with other banks and finance companies advertising themselves as national companies, Johnson said others have the no documentation mortage as a fill-in product but GreenPoint has made the product its specialty and is "geared to competing very aggressively."

He also said credit quality in the product compares favorably with the mortgage market in general. "This product has a relatively high default rate because of the increased risk that we take on, but the losses are not great because we get very big down payments."

Johnson said GreenPoint has also benefited from its focus on raising deposits in just one geographic area. He said average deposits per branch are a hefty $150 million. After the Home Savings branch acquisition some branches have been pruned reducing the total to 76 from 84. Some high cost deposits have been allowed to run off, he said.
"We have the luxury of allowing the bank to get a little bit smaller in order to be able to minimize the cost of money to us," he said.

Asked how the company manages its interest rate risk, Johnson responded, "Basically, what we do is hedge new production as carefully as we can. This year all of our fixed rate production is hedged either through interest rate swaps or through the sale of long duration fixed rate investment securities so that we are not adding to risk as we are adding to our assets."

GreenPoint also reports cash earnings which add goodwill charges from acquisitions to reported earnings. Fourth-quarter core cash earnings were $1.15 per share versus $0.77 a year ago. --(Cal Mankowski/New York Newsdesk/212 859 1732)--
